attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, stated in his voice.

semantics.note: Unhedged present-tense claim about ChatGPT in 2024. Turning 'bullshit' into fabricated content is a fair reading. The 'as strong as ever' comparison is kept.

contract.note: Splitting the claim into (a) fabricating instead of declining and (b) no weaker than at launch is the ordinary literal reading of 'as strong as ever'. Whether that phrase is rhetoric or a literal comparison decides part (b), as the contract's flags say.

evidence.note: Independent Tow Center audit from November 2024. ChatGPT search rarely admitted it could not answer and gave wrong answers 153 times out of 200. This supports part (a).

OpenAI's own March 2023 figures: GPT-4 scored 40% higher than GPT-3.5 on internal factuality tests. This goes against part (b), but it comes from the company, not an independent check, and it compares GPT-4 with the latest GPT-3.5, not launch-day ChatGPT.

reviews.rationale: Part (a) holds. An independent November 2024 audit shows ChatGPT making up answers rather than declining. Part (b), that the tendency is no weaker than at launch, is contradicted by OpenAI's own evaluations showing big factuality gains from GPT-3.5 to GPT-4. That counterevidence comes from the company and no study compares the launch model with the 2024 model directly, so it is weaker, but it still counts against the literal comparison.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: 'This' refers to the mitigations he names just before: scaling, RAG, and system-prompt instructions. The proposition keeps that scope.

contract.note: The plain reading, that no method had brought hallucinations to zero or near zero, is the ordinary meaning of 'eliminated'. That bar favours the speaker, but it is fair.

evidence.note: Shows that vendors had claimed RAG 'eliminated' hallucinations. That is background, not evidence of the outcome.
Preregistered study from May 2024: leading RAG legal tools still hallucinated 17–33% of the time. This falls inside the target period.

OpenAI's own system card lists clearly non-zero hallucination rates for GPT-4o and o1-preview on SimpleQA and PersonQA. It was published after the post, but it describes models from the target period, and a company admitting flaws in its own models carries weight.

reviews.rationale: In 2024 both scaled frontier models and RAG products still had substantial hallucination rates, far from zero. Nothing in the packet shows any of the mitigations reaching near-zero hallucination. There is no measurement specific to Apple's prompt, but the claim is met by the scaling and RAG evidence.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The revised proposition keeps the 'pretty much' qualifier, the factuality scope and his 'wishing and hoping' framing. Calling factuality 'the most important question' is a value judgment and correctly left ungraded.

contract.note: Reading the claim as 'little substantive improvement' is an ordinary reading. But 'wishing and hoping' could also mean outputs still can't be trusted in practice, and which reading is used decides the outcome, as the contract itself notes.

evidence.note: Peer-reviewed study from 2023: fabricated citations fell from 55% with GPT-3.5 to 18% with GPT-4. That is real improvement, but it does not cover the contract's November 2022 to November 2024 endpoints.
Precision barely changed between GPT-3.5-Turbo and GPT-4-Turbo (90.8 vs 91.7), while recall and F1 improved. The GPT-3.5 tested is the January 2024 snapshot, not the launch model.

reviews.rationale: The contract asks for matched evaluations of launch-era ChatGPT against systems from November 2024. The packet has none. The available studies point in different directions: big drops in citation fabrication, but almost flat factual precision. Neither matches the required endpoints, so the evidence does not settle whether there was little substantive improvement.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the hedged 'may have declined', which is not scored, alongside the firm 'certainly haven't vanished', which is scored.

contract.note: The contract scores only the firm part, that hallucinations were still present in 2024 LLMs. That is the ordinary reading, and the hedged part is properly left unscored.

evidence.note: Benchmark paper from October 2024 documents GPT-4o inventing a link between a song and an album while summarizing a passage. That is a hallucination by a current model inside the target period.

reviews.rationale: The firm part of the claim is that hallucinations had not vanished. A documented GPT-4o hallucination from 2024 is enough to establish that, and nothing in the packet suggests hallucinations had been eliminated. The hedged 'may have declined' is not scored.
